what_it_does: Modern GPUs have multiple types of compute engines: scalar units (for single-value operations), vector units (for parallel operations on arrays), and tensor cores (the GPU's specialized arithmetic units optimized for matrix multiplies). Current compilers map an entire tensor operation to just one unit type, leaving the others idle. This paper introduces a technique called iTex (instruction-level texture) tessellation that breaks a computation into heterogeneous sub-tiles, assigning each to the most appropriate unit. For example, one part of a matrix operation might run on tensor cores while an adjacent part runs on vector units simultaneously, doubling the work done per cycle. The compiler automatically figures out the optimal tiling strategy.
